key_insight: SteelAgent’s apparent prediction accuracy and uncertainty reliability drop sharply when evaluation holds out unfamiliar steel families or data sources.
engineering_relevance: Steel property estimates and compliance scores should identify the evaluation population before informing alloy selection or inverse design.
method: Combine metallurgical descriptors and machine-learning models with an LLM interface.
Audit generalization using random, steel-family and source-held-out evaluations.
Assess prediction-interval coverage, physics-feature effects and group-level errors.
evidence_signal: Gradient-boosting pooled out-of-fold R² fell from 0.859 on random splits to 0.113 with steel-family holdouts; nominal 90% interval coverage was 91.0% under random splitting but 37.6% on held-out sources.
watch_item: Physics-derived features were not consistently beneficial: gradient-boosting R² increased by 0.2534 in a 17-family holdout analysis but decreased by 0.358 in a separate four-grade laboratory analysis.
paper_title: SteelAgent: LLM-Orchestrated, Physics-Informed Steel Property Prediction with Audited Generalization and Calibrated Uncertainty
